subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Central Park: Nature by Design
description: A fast breakdown of Central Park: Nature by Design for builders.

hook.text: Central Park looks natural. Nothing about it is. Every rock, hill, and lake was placed by hand in the 1860s.

buildup.text: Olmsted and Vaux won a design competition. Their plan required moving 10 million cartloads of earth.

discovery.text: Building the park displaced 1,600 residents, including Seneca Village — a thriving Black community.

twist.text: Today Central Park generates $1 billion annually for the surrounding economy and raises nearby rents by 20%.

climax.text: The park survived plans for highways, parking lots, and a stadium. Citizens fought off every threat.

punchline.text: Built by destroying a neighborhood. Saved by defending green space.

quiz.question: What community was displaced to build Central Park?
options: Little Italy, a neighborhood of Italian immigrants
Seneca Village, a thriving Black community
Five Points, an overcrowded immigrant settlement
